text: Swimming involves many skills, one of which is the use of goggles. Goggles are worn by swimmers to protect their eyes and keep water out. They are usually made of a lightweight, flexible material that is designed to fit snugly over the swimmer's head. Goggles can help prevent eye irritation or injury from water, and can also help reduce drag and improve performance in the water. Another important skill in swimming is the ability to perform laps, which involves swimming continuously in a specific distance or time. Laps can be performed in a variety of swimming strokes, including freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, and butterfly, and can be practiced either in the water or on a poolside lane. With practice and dedication, anyone can learn to swim and perform laps effectively.
